questions: When I'm walking, I deliberately notice the sensations of my body moving.

I criticize myself for having irrational or inappropriate emotions.

I tell myself that I shouldn't be feeling the way I'm feeling.
I notice how food and drink affect my thoughts, bodily sensations, and emotions.

I am easily distracted.
I believe some of my thoughts are abnormal or bad, and I shouldn't think that way.

I have trouble finding the right words to express how I feel about things.
I make judgments about whether my thoughts are good or bad.

factors.name: Observing
factors.description: The ability to notice, attend to, and track external and internal experience: feelings, emotions, thoughts, sounds, smells, and sensations.

factors.name: Describing
factors.description: The ability to label inner experiences with words.

factors.name: Acting with Awareness
factors.description: The ability to be fully present in the here and now, engaged with the current moment, instead of operating on autopilot.

factors.name: Non-Judging of Inner Experience
factors.description: The ability to accept any inner experience — even painful ones — as they are, without labeling them as unwanted, and without striving to get rid of or suppress them.

factors.name: Non-Reactivity to Inner Experience
factors.description: The ability to allow thoughts and feelings to come and go without getting caught up in or carried away by them.
